overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session under Purpose 7, but ordered amended, more detailed November 7 executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session on Nov. 7 to discuss a client's physician profile dispute without 48 hours' notice, arguing it should have used Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that, because Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 111, section 53B and Chapter 112, section 5 require that 53B Reports remain confidential, the Board properly convened in executive session under Purpose 7 to discuss the profile disputes with respect to information contained in the 53B Reports.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; the AG reviewed the Nov. 7 executive session minutes in camera and found them insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes are inadequate to meet the standard required by the Open Meeting Law because they do not offer a sufficiently detailed summary of the Board's discussions, and instead simply state that the Board considered the profile disputes and the recommendation of a staff member.

remedy: Amend the November 7 executive session meeting minutes to comply with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
Certify to the AG within sixty days of the letter that the executive session minutes have been amended.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to amend its November 7 executive session meeting minutes in accordance with the requirements of G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
